title: Max Verstappen’s 2026 F1 season start gets worse. His car is ‘undriveable’ at the Chinese GP
content:
SHANGHAI, China — Max Verstappen says Red Bull’s 2026 Formula 1 car is “completely undriveable” and that “every lap is like survival” after a difficult Saturday at the Chinese Grand Prix.

Four-time world champion Verstappen finished ninth in the sprint race at the Shanghai International Circuit after struggling to get off the line and falling as low as 15th position at the end of the first lap of 19. He then clawed his way back up the order to finish ninth.

The 28-year-old then qualified down in eighth place for Sunday’s grand prix, finishing almost one second behind pole-sitter Kimi Antonelli of Mercedes.

“We changed quite a lot on the car (after the sprint) and it made zero difference,” Verstappen told reporters after qualifying in China.

“The whole weekend we’ve been off. The car is completely undriveable. I cannot even put a bit of a reference in. Every lap is like survival.”

It continued a miserable start to Verstappen’s season after he crashed in qualifying last Saturday in Australia. The shunt was caused by a sudden locking of the rear axle on his car, and meant he started way down the order in Melbourne before Verstappen recovered to sixth place.

Verstappen said on Saturday in Shanghai that Red Bull had taken a step back with its RB22 car’s performance compared to the Australian weekend, but said “we know now at least that the balance is really disconnected” given his form in China.

Verstappen’s teammate, Isack Hadjar, 21, qualified ninth for Sunday’s Chinese GP. The French driver finished a further one-tenth of a second behind Verstappen’s best time.

Red Bull entered 2026 with a brand-new engine that it designed in-house for the first time in its history. This had prompted the team to downplay expectations ahead of the season given the scale of setting up such an ambitious project.

Verstappen said that while the engine’s performance contributed a little bit to his current lack of headline results, he said it was “probably not the biggest (element)” to explain his Shanghai struggles.

“We lose so much from the car at the moment around here,” Verstappen said, referring to his car’s poor handling and excessive sliding around the Shanghai lap. “Plus also, I cannot push at all, because the car doesn’t let me. That’s why I don’t really feel in control of the car.

“It’s just really not how it should be.”

Verstappen has been an outspoken critic of F1’s new cars, which place a far greater emphasis on electrical power from the battery in the hybrid engine producing a car’s overall power.

In preseason testing in Bahrain last month, he called this “anti-racing” and “like Formula E on steroids.” Formula E is another single seater motorsport category where the cars are powered by an all-electric drivetrain.

On Saturday in China, Verstappen said: “From Lap 1 of these new regulations, I’ve not enjoyed this car, for sure.”

Red Bull lacked the outright performance in Shanghai qualifying of the leading Mercedes, Ferrari and McLaren cars, which locked out the front three rows of the grid. But Alpine’s Pierre Gasly also managed to outqualify Verstappen, taking seventh on the grid.

When asked what result may be possible to achieve in the race on Sunday, Verstappen replied: “Where I’m at (on the grid). It’s not going to be a fun race.”
